name: (d,g)-cage order
definition: For fixed degree d and girth g, find the smallest order n of a d-regular graph of girth exactly g.
solution_format: Adjacency list/matrix of a d-regular graph with a verifiable girth certificate; objective is vertex count.
human_baseline: Exoo, Jajcay, Goedgebeur et al. (2025 preprint) improved eleven upper bounds; e.g. n(4,10)≤320. Exoo–Jajcay (2013) survey distinguishes known cages from upper-bound constructions; optimality is proved only for some parameter pairs.
verification_cost: Medium for a supplied graph; high to prove global minimality.
risks: Report incumbent order separately from proven minimum; exact optimality certificates are often absent.
reason: Natural scalar objective, rich named record tables, and independently checkable graph witnesses.

name: Degree–diameter problem
definition: For maximum degree d and diameter k, maximize the order of a simple graph.
solution_format: Graph adjacency list plus proof/check of maximum degree and diameter; objective vertex count.
human_baseline: The large degree/diameter graph table (Miller, Širáň and contributors; updated tables) records best known orders and marks the few proven optimal cases; Moore bound is an upper bound, not an attained baseline.
verification_cost: Medium for witness; exact optimum usually unknown.
risks: Must label best-known vs proven; table updates and graph conventions (regular vs maximum degree) need freezing.
reason: A clear extremal objective and extensive human constructions; feasible to score witness size.

name: Classical Ramsey number lower-bound construction
definition: For fixed s,t, construct the largest N-vertex graph with neither an s-clique nor an independent t-set, equivalently improve the lower bound R(s,t)≥N+1.
solution_format: Graph adjacency list; independently verify forbidden-clique/independent-set conditions; scalar N.
human_baseline: Exoo et al. (1997) catalogued 656 nonisomorphic (5,5,42)-graphs, implying R(5,5)≥43; Radziszowski Dynamic Survey rev. 18 (2026) records 43≤R(5,5)≤46, with the upper bound by Angeltveit–McKay (2024).
verification_cost: High; exact clique and independence checks scale exponentially, though certificates are finite and reproducible.
risks: A one-unit increase is meaningful but only if exact validation is performed; do not score heuristic estimates or claim exact Ramsey values from a lower-bound witness.
reason: Excellent human baseline and natural scalar, but restrict to modest s,t and require exact verifier/certificate.

name: Graph Ramsey number R(G,H)
definition: Minimum N such that every red/blue coloring of K_N contains red G or blue H; candidates can instead give certified lower-bound colorings on N−1 vertices.
solution_format: Edge coloring of K_N−1; objective largest certified coloring order.
human_baseline: Radziszowski Dynamic Survey DS1 (rev. 18, 2026) and Exoo construction tables contain published values and lower-bound colorings.
verification_cost: High but finite for lower-bound witness; exact value requires separate upper-bound proof.
risks: Overlaps classical Ramsey task; keep only non-clique forbidden graphs if parameterized as a distinct task family. Exact score cannot be claimed from coloring alone.
reason: Strong literature, but merge with classical Ramsey unless benchmark specifically fixes arbitrary graph pairs.

name: Turán number ex(n,K_r)
definition: Maximize edges in an n-vertex K_r-free graph.
solution_format: Simple graph adjacency list; objective edge count.
human_baseline: Turán's theorem (1941) exactly gives the balanced complete (r−1)-partite graph and edge count for all n,r; a calibration item with a formula, not a frontier challenge.
verification_cost: Low for candidate graph; proving optimality is theorem-level but formula is known.
risks: Too formulaic for a discovery benchmark; use only calibration, not novelty leaderboard.
reason: Natural scalar and exact human baseline, but classic cases have closed-form solutions.

name: Zarankiewicz number Z_{s,t}(m,n)
definition: Maximize edges in a bipartite graph with part sizes m,n containing no K_{s,t}.
solution_format: Bipartite adjacency matrix; objective number of 1 entries.
human_baseline: Published exact values and bounds are surveyed in the extremal graph literature; small square cases have SAT-verified tables (Mubayi et al. / 2022 SAT study corrects known table errors). Explicit finite-field constructions give human lower bounds.
verification_cost: Medium for forbidden biclique and edge count; optimality high.
risks: Older tables contain errors; pin a source version and instance. General asymptotics remain open.
reason: Clean extremal scalar, abundant constructions, and small instances admit exact machine checks.

name: Hypergraph Turán number ex_r(n,F)
definition: Maximize edges in an r-uniform n-vertex hypergraph avoiding a fixed forbidden r-graph F.
solution_format: List of r-subsets; objective edge count.
human_baseline: Keevash's survey and the Erdős problems archive record open cases and constructions. The 3-uniform K4 problem has Turán's construction at density 5/9, but exact density remains open; finite n entries can have exact/conjectured distinctions.
verification_cost: High; checking F-freeness is manageable for small n, global optimality is difficult.
risks: Do not blur finite exact values with asymptotic Turán density; choose frozen small n and explicit F.
reason: Canonical research problem with natural edge-count objective and published constructions/bounds.

name: Graph saturation number sat(n,F)
definition: Minimize edges in an n-vertex F-saturated graph: it is F-free, but adding any missing edge creates F.
solution_format: Graph adjacency list; objective edge count.
human_baseline: Bollobás (1965) initiated the problem; for cliques, classical constructions and recent papers give exact formulas for many ranges. Current papers state the standard definition and bounds.
verification_cost: Medium for candidate; exact optimum often requires proof.
risks: Newer specific F parameter results must be checked against publication status; easy families have formulaic answers.
reason: Natural minimization objective with established theory; curate a small frozen set of nontrivial F,n cases.

name: Maximum order of a Ramsey (s,t)-graph
definition: For fixed s,t, maximize n such that a graph on n vertices has clique number <s and independence number <t.
solution_format: Graph adjacency matrix; objective order n.
human_baseline: McKay's ANU computational Ramsey database includes explicit graphs and describes the largest known Ramsey graphs; the optimum is R(s,t)−1.
verification_cost: High for maximality; graph witness checks can be expensive.
risks: Equivalent to classical Ramsey lower-bound construction; merge into that row to avoid duplicate benchmark.
reason: Duplicate formulation of the same Ramsey objective; retain one canonical task.

name: Small regular graph of given girth (cage variants)
definition: Construct a small d-regular graph of girth at least g, possibly with extra restrictions such as bipartite or vertex-transitive.
solution_format: Graph; minimize order.
human_baseline: Exoo–Jajcay dynamic cage survey and House of Graphs record tables catalog constructions, with restrictions treated separately in papers.
verification_cost: Medium.
risks: This is the cage family; do not count variants as separate tasks unless added restriction is canonical and independently studied.
reason: Parameter/restriction variants of the cage task should be merged.

name: Maximum edges under prescribed girth
definition: For fixed n and girth threshold g, maximize edges in an n-vertex graph with girth at least g.
solution_format: Graph adjacency list; objective edge count.
human_baseline: Erdős–Sachs (1963) established existence of regular graphs of prescribed degree and girth; the cage survey provides named extremal records, but exact max-edge records for this broader fixed-n formulation were not curated in this pass.
verification_cost: Medium for girth and edge count; optimum difficult.
risks: A general problem family with sparse centralized records; source and exact instance baseline still need checking.
reason: Broad formulation lacks a verified standard human record table; cage records cover the stronger canonical family.

name: Maximum independence number under graph constraints
definition: Given a fixed graph class or forbidden subgraph family and order n, maximize alpha(G).
solution_format: Graph witness; objective independence number.
human_baseline: Many individual extremal results exist, but no unified, verified baseline database for arbitrary constraints was established in this survey pass.
verification_cost: High: exact maximum independent set is NP-hard; validating claimed alpha needs a matching upper certificate.
risks: Too broad; do not score a heuristic alpha estimate as exact.
reason: No single canonical family or practical human baseline; verification burden is high.

name: Saturated graph construction for fixed F
definition: Find an F-saturated graph with few edges on n vertices.
solution_format: Graph witness; objective edge count.
human_baseline: See sat(n,F) literature, but duplicates the saturation number task.
verification_cost: Medium.
risks: Duplicate formulation.
reason: Merge into canonical saturation-number task.

name: Covering number C(v,k,t)
definition: Find the fewest k-subsets of a v-set such that every t-subset is included in at least one selected block.
solution_format: List of k-subsets; objective block count.
human_baseline: La Jolla Combinatorics Repository (Dan Gordon; frozen 2026) stores tens of thousands of best-known covers and lower bounds; individual construction records identify contributors/methods.
verification_cost: Low-medium for coverage; proving minimum needs lower bound.
risks: Repository baseline may be best-known rather than optimum; freeze data snapshot and preserve authorship metadata.
reason: One of the strongest candidates: standardized finite objects, natural scalar, and large human record corpus.

name: Covering array CAN(t,k,v)
definition: Minimize rows N of a k-column v-ary array so every t selected columns contain every v^t tuple at least once.
solution_format: N×k array over v symbols; objective N.
human_baseline: NIST Covering Array Library lists actual arrays for strengths 2–6 and 2–6 levels, plus best-known sizes to 20,000 columns (strength 2) and 10,000 (strengths 3–6); NIST and Colbourn records are human constructions/bounds.
verification_cost: Low for explicit array; minimum proof varies.
risks: Keep uniform alphabet case separate from variable-strength/general mixed-level variants; NIST best-known size tables do not always include arrays.
reason: Excellent benchmark corpus and easily verifiable scalar optimization.

name: Orthogonal array minimum-run construction
definition: For fixed strength t, levels and columns, construct an orthogonal array with the fewest rows (or maximize columns for fixed rows), each t-column tuple appearing equally often.
solution_format: Array with explicit index lambda; objective rows or columns, with one direction fixed per instance.
human_baseline: Neil Sloane's library contains 200+ explicit arrays; Eendebak–Schoen catalogue complete non-isomorphic arrays for selected small parameters. OA( N,k,s,t) must meet divisibility/Rao bounds.
verification_cost: Low for explicit array; minimality moderate/high.
risks: Do not conflate OA existence, maximum columns, and minimum-run objectives; fix one scalar per instance. Strength-2 binary OAs are essentially Hadamard matrices.
reason: Curated human constructions and simple exact validator; good if objective/configuration are fixed consistently.

name: Steiner system block construction S(t,k,v)
definition: Construct k-subsets so each t-subset occurs in exactly one block; the number of blocks is forced by parameters when divisibility holds.
solution_format: Block list; scalar objective may be block count only if allowing a relaxed/partial design.
scalar_objective: none for exact Steiner existence (block count is forced)
human_baseline: La Jolla repository links Steiner systems; classical systems (projective planes, Witt designs) have named constructions and authors.
verification_cost: Low for incidence verification.
risks: Exact existence is boolean and has no optimization scalar; block count is fixed by counting.
reason: Fails scalar optimization requirement; can be included only as validation/calibration, not scored task.

name: Packing number D(v,k,t)
definition: Maximize the number of k-subsets on v points such that no t-subset is contained in more than one block.
solution_format: List of blocks; objective block count.
human_baseline: La Jolla covering repository focuses on coverings, while classical packing bounds and constructions are published; candidate instance-level records require dedicated database/source review.
verification_cost: Low for packing property.
risks: No unified current record table confirmed in this pass; may overlap partial Steiner designs.
reason: Good scalar and verification, but human-record baseline needs further curation.

name: Social golfer maximum schedule length
definition: Partition players into groups of fixed size each round, avoiding any pair meeting twice; maximize number of rounds.
solution_format: Round-by-round partitions; objective number of rounds.
human_baseline: CSPLib problem 010 defines the canonical 32 golfers in groups of four and its generalization; published constraint-programming literature reports solved/optimal schedules for small parameter sets, but benchmark records need per-instance capture.
verification_cost: Low for pair uniqueness; maximality requires a bound/proof.
risks: Could degenerate into mere feasibility when target rounds fixed; use maximize rounds and instances with documented human optima.
reason: Natural schedule objective and benchmark tradition, but require verified per-instance baseline.

name: Maximum number of mutually orthogonal Latin squares
definition: For order n, maximize the number of pairwise orthogonal Latin squares (MOLS).
solution_format: List of Latin squares; objective count.
human_baseline: Bruck–Ryser–Chowla gives nonexistence restrictions; complete values are known for several small orders, while the standard MOLS tables record constructions and bounds.
verification_cost: Low for square/orthogonality checks; maximality often hard.
risks: Exact optimum open for some n; source table version and proof status must be frozen.
reason: Canonical extremal design quantity, simple verifier, and substantive human theory.

name: Maximum Hadamard matrix order under a bound
definition: For a fixed search bound M, find the largest order h≤M for which a ±1 matrix has mutually orthogonal rows.
solution_format: Hadamard matrix; scalar order h.
human_baseline: Sloane maintains a library of Hadamard matrices and known orders; Hadamard's determinant bound requires order 1,2 or divisible by 4 above 2, and many orders are constructed by Sylvester/Paley methods.
verification_cost: Low for witness; proving no larger allowed order is number-theoretic or exhaustive.
risks: Avoid fixed-order existence boolean benchmark; choose maximize order under a fixed cap and compare with curated library.
reason: Fixed-instance feasibility is boolean; maximizing order under an arbitrary cap is not a natural standalone optimization benchmark.

name: Projective plane order search
definition: For a fixed cap q≤Q, find the largest order q for which a projective plane exists.
solution_format: Incidence matrix; scalar order q.
human_baseline: Prime-power orders have finite-field constructions; Bruck–Ryser (1949) excludes some orders; Lam, Thiel & Swiercz (1989) computationally proved no plane of order 10 exists.
verification_cost: Low for candidate incidence structure; nonexistence proof can be extremely expensive.
risks: Underlying task often asks existence at fixed q, a boolean; bounded maximize-q wrapper is artificial and dominated by known prime-power formula.
reason: Mostly existence and known algebraic construction; poor natural scalar task.

name: Optimal Golomb ruler length
definition: For m integer marks, place distinct marks so all positive pairwise differences are distinct and minimize the largest mark.
solution_format: Increasing integer mark list starting at 0; objective final mark.
human_baseline: Shearer (1990) exhaustively proved optimal lengths 127,151,177 for m=14,15,16; distributed.net completed proof of optimality through m=28 (2022 records), and CSPLib has the standard benchmark. Distinguish proven optima from larger-m best known rulers.
verification_cost: Low for ruler; optimality proof high for large m.
risks: Open sizes beyond proven range must be scored as incumbent length, not as proven optimum; preserve provenance and certificate status.
reason: Ideal scalar objective, a standard benchmark and exceptionally clear historical human record.

name: Difference triangle sets
definition: Construct several rows of marks with all within-row positive differences distinct globally; minimize maximum span under fixed row/mark counts.
solution_format: Rows of integer marks; objective maximum row span.
human_baseline: Published difference-triangle-set constructions and tabu search literature report best-known spans; Golomb rulers are the one-row special case.
verification_cost: Low for a witness.
risks: Overlaps Golomb ruler at r=1; careful definition variants (all differences vs row-tagged) must be frozen.
reason: A legitimate adjacent optimization family with published records, but merge one-row case into Golomb rulers.

name: Largest Sidon set in [n]
definition: Find the largest subset of {1,…,n} whose pairwise sums of distinct elements are all different (equivalently distinct positive differences).
solution_format: Sorted integer set; objective cardinality.
human_baseline: Erdős–Turán (1941) prove the maximum Sidon-set size in [n] is asymptotic to √n; Bose–Chowla (1962) give finite-field constructions. Specific finite-n exact maxima are not asserted here; use a verified construction/bound table before scoring exactness.
verification_cost: Low for witness; proof of maximum can be difficult.
risks: Terminology differs on allowing repeated summands; specify pairwise sums of distinct elements and distinct differences explicitly. Exact small-n baseline table still needs verification.
reason: Very natural scalar and classical constructions; source-level exact benchmark table needs checking.

name: Maximum cap set in F_3^n
definition: Find a largest subset of the vector space F_3^n containing no affine line (three distinct points summing to zero).
solution_format: Point list in F_3^n; objective cardinality.
human_baseline: Pellegrino (1970) proved maximum 20 for n=4. Kleinberg–Sawin–Speyer (2016) gave constructions and Ellenberg–Gijswijt (2017) exponential upper bound; human lower-bound records are published for higher n, with exact values limited.
verification_cost: Low for witness and no-line property; proving optimality difficult.
risks: Modern record tables may have changed; distinguish exact small dimensions from best-known lower bounds.
reason: Canonical additive extremal problem, clear point-count objective, and unusually visible human construction frontier.

name: Largest 3-term-progression-free subset of [n]
definition: Find a largest subset of {1,…,n} containing no nontrivial 3-term arithmetic progression.
solution_format: Integer set; objective cardinality.
human_baseline: Behrend (1946) gave classical constructions; exact small-n values are known computationally and Roth's theorem gives qualitative upper bounds. Pin exact-value source/version for each n.
verification_cost: Low for witness, exponential for maximality.
risks: Closely related to cap sets but distinct ambient group; avoid treating parameter variants as different tasks.
reason: Natural cardinality objective, but benchmark exact records need authoritative tables and manageable n.

name: Minimum difference basis for [n]
definition: Find a smallest set A of integers such that every integer 1,…,n is a difference of two elements of A.
solution_format: Sorted integer set; objective cardinality (or span if a different canonical version is chosen).
human_baseline: Difference-basis literature has asymptotic bounds and specific constructions (Rédei–Rényi; Leech), but this pass did not verify an accessible modern exact-record table.
verification_cost: Low for coverage; proving minimality difficult.
risks: Several inequivalent definitions (difference set vs difference basis, interval endpoint, signed differences); human baseline source requires additional research.
reason: Natural minimum-cardinality task but needs definition and authoritative record table curation.

name: Minimum additive basis of order h for [n]
definition: Find a smallest A⊂[0,m] or minimum largest element such that every target integer up to n is a sum of h elements of A (convention fixed).
solution_format: Integer set; objective cardinality or maximum element (choose one).
human_baseline: Classical additive-basis literature studies several nonequivalent variants; a specific finite database and baseline were not verified in this pass.
verification_cost: Low-medium for witness; proof of optimality hard.
risks: Too many incompatible objectives/conventions; no source-backed fixed record table.
reason: Insufficiently canonical and no verified human baseline.

name: Maximum sum-free subset of a finite group
definition: Maximize |A| in a fixed finite abelian group subject to no x,y,z∈A with x+y=z (convention fixed).
solution_format: Element list; objective cardinality.
human_baseline: For integers [n], the maximum is floor((n+1)/2), giving an exact calibration; finite group extremal classifications are known in many cases.
verification_cost: Low for witness, exact optimum varies.
risks: Integer interval is formulaic; broad finite-group versions need more specific literature and are not one task.
reason: Useful calibration only for interval case; broader version lacks canonical benchmark instances.

name: Sum-difference sets in finite groups
definition: For a fixed finite group G and target coverage convention, find a small set A with A+A−A=G or maximize prescribed sum/difference coverage.
solution_format: Subset A; scalar size or uncovered count only if established optimization target.
human_baseline: Several related sum-difference problems occur in additive combinatorics, but no canonical single finite optimization record/database was verified here.
verification_cost: Low for a fixed definition.
risks: Name covers inequivalent problems; would risk inventing a benchmark objective.
reason: No canonical objective or verifiable standard human baseline found.

name: Costas array maximal order
definition: Find a largest order n with a permutation whose displacement vectors are all distinct (Costas array).
solution_format: Permutation; objective order n under a fixed search bound.
human_baseline: Costas arrays are tabulated by order and constructions (Welch, Golomb) are published; finite existence records are maintained by specialist databases.
verification_cost: Low for witness; proving nonexistence at larger order is difficult.
risks: Fixed-order form is boolean; bounded maximize-order form may collapse to known constructions. Need a verified authoritative record table.
reason: Fixed-instance feasibility is boolean; maximizing order under an arbitrary cap is not a natural standalone optimization benchmark.

name: Cyclic difference set construction
definition: Find a k-subset of a cyclic group of order v whose nonzero differences cover each nonzero group element exactly lambda times.
solution_format: Residue set; no free scalar because v,k,lambda determine size.
human_baseline: La Jolla hosts difference-set data and classical Singer constructions provide examples.
verification_cost: Low.
risks: Fixed-parameter existence is boolean; parameters determine the construction size.
reason: No natural optimization scalar for fixed parameters.

name: Maximum order weighing matrix under bound
definition: For a fixed order cap and weight ratio/structural class, find the largest order of a weighing matrix W with WWᵀ=kI.
solution_format: Matrix entries 0,±1; scalar order.
human_baseline: Dan Gordon's La Jolla data include circulant weighing matrices and record constructions.
verification_cost: Low for witness; existence/nonexistence frontier varies.
risks: Different matrix classes and weights must be separated; database data scope needs review.
reason: Fixed-instance feasibility is boolean; maximizing order under an arbitrary cap is not a natural standalone optimization benchmark.

name: Maximum matching-free hypergraph extremal number
definition: Maximize edges in an r-uniform n-vertex hypergraph with matching number below fixed s.
solution_format: Hyperedge list; objective edge count.
human_baseline: Erdős matching conjecture and extensive exact results give canonical bounds; recent papers prove exact ranges, but there is no single table verified in this pass.
verification_cost: Medium for matching number at small n; optimum proof hard.
risks: Be careful whether Berge matching or disjoint hyperedges; family has multiple conventions.
reason: Natural extremal scalar, but needs a canonical instance table and definition pinning.

name: Hypergraph Ramsey lower-bound construction
definition: For fixed uniformity and target monochromatic hypergraphs, construct a large coloring avoiding both, maximizing vertex/order count.
solution_format: Coloring of complete uniform hypergraph; objective number of vertices.
human_baseline: Radziszowski's Dynamic Survey records classical hypergraph Ramsey values and bounds.
verification_cost: Very high for larger instances; exhaustive edge coloring verification grows rapidly.
risks: Overlaps general Ramsey construction; high validation cost and sparse human records.
reason: Merge with Ramsey task and restrict if retained; poor standalone scalability.

name: Minimum covering code size K_q(n,R)
definition: Find the fewest q-ary length-n words whose Hamming balls of radius R cover the whole space.
solution_format: Codeword list; objective code size.
human_baseline: Published covering-code tables (Hill, Heden and collaborators) record lower and upper bounds and constructions; an authoritative unified current database was not verified in this pass.
verification_cost: Low for full coverage at small n; proof of minimum difficult.
risks: Source table needs primary-source verification; coding theory scope may overlap another benchmark category.
reason: Excellent finite scalar optimization, but baseline database must be sourced and frozen.

name: Maximum clique on standard named graph instances
definition: Find a maximum clique in a fixed published graph instance.
solution_format: Vertex set; objective clique cardinality.
human_baseline: DIMACS challenge graph collection and exact solver literature contain known optimum values for instances.
verification_cost: High; membership proves lower bound but maximum requires certificate.
risks: Generic algorithmic benchmark rather than mathematical construction discovery; graph names/instances are inputs, not a coherent theorem family.
reason: Optimization is canonical but fails the intended construction-discovery flavor and exact upper-certificate burden.

name: Maximum independent set on standard named graph instances
definition: Find a maximum independent vertex set in a fixed graph from a published benchmark suite.
solution_format: Vertex set; objective cardinality.
human_baseline: DIMACS challenge collection and exact graph algorithms provide incumbent and optimum records for selected instances.
verification_cost: High for optimality certificate.
risks: Generic solver task, not a named mathematical construction family.
reason: Does not fit mathematical construction benchmark goal; duplicates optimization contest category.

name: Extremal linear hypergraph with forbidden configuration
definition: Maximize edges in a linear r-uniform hypergraph avoiding a fixed small configuration, e.g. a linear cycle.
solution_format: Hyperedge list; objective edge count.
human_baseline: Keevash's survey and published linear-cycle Turán results give exact large-n ranges and constructions for many r,F.
verification_cost: Medium for F-free check.
risks: Broad family; choose a single standard F such as linear cycle and verify exact finite-n human records.
reason: Natural optimization with active research, though overlaps broad hypergraph Turán task.

name: Maximum partial Steiner triple system
definition: Choose as many triples on v points as possible with no pair repeated; equivalently packing number D(v,3,2).
solution_format: Triple list; objective number of triples.
human_baseline: Classical packing theory gives near-perfect packings and leave classifications; should be merged with the general packing-design family and source exact records per v.
verification_cost: Low.
risks: Equivalent to packing design with t=2,k=3; do not count as separate benchmark.
reason: Parameter specialization of packing-design task.

name: Largest cap/arc in finite projective plane
definition: For a fixed finite projective plane, maximize a point set meeting each line in at most a prescribed number of points (arc/cap variants).
solution_format: Point set; cardinality objective.
human_baseline: Finite geometry literature and databases catalogue arcs/caps and complete classifications for small orders; no specific public primary database was verified in this pass.
verification_cost: Low for witness; maximality high.
risks: Terminology and projective plane choice vary; needs specific named family and baseline records.
reason: Promising finite-geometry extremal objective but evidence/source curation incomplete.

name: Orthogonal Latin square existence
definition: Find a pair of orthogonal Latin squares of fixed order n.
solution_format: Pair of squares; no free scalar.
human_baseline: Known constructions and nonexistence results are published; Euler's 36 officers problem is a named nonexistence example.
verification_cost: Low for positive witness.
risks: Fixed-order feasibility has no scalar objective.
reason: Boolean existence task violates scalar-objective constraint.

name: Complete MOLS count by order
definition: For each order n, report the maximum number N(n) of mutually orthogonal Latin squares.
solution_format: List of MOLS; objective count.
human_baseline: Same mathematical quantity as maximum MOLS, with standard constructions and Bruck–Ryser–Chowla restrictions.
verification_cost: Low for witness, maximality hard.
risks: Duplicate naming of MOLS task.
reason: Merge with maximum mutually orthogonal Latin squares.

name: Anti-Ramsey coloring number
definition: For fixed graph H and host K_n, maximize distinct edge colors while requiring every H-copy to be rainbow-free (or the converse standard anti-Ramsey convention).
solution_format: Edge coloring; objective number of colors.
human_baseline: Anti-Ramsey literature gives exact results for selected host/pattern families, but a unified record table and canonical convention were not verified.
verification_cost: Medium for fixed finite coloring.
risks: Definition conventions vary; no verified broad human baseline.
reason: Insufficiently canonical and weak baseline evidence for benchmark curation.
